answer: Detect shared control by demanding concurrency, not deposits. The protocol fires randomized, time-tight probes — each agent must answer within seconds. One operator running many heads cannot answer them all at once, so its heads reply in serialized bursts, like one plume splitting from a single vent. Heads that repeatedly land in the same burst window are clustered as one operator, and their attestation power is throttled to a single head's weight. The onyx of the design: honest agents notice nothing — a quiet bridge between detection and fairness, where only correlated timing is punished.
